Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The MiG-17 was license-built in China as the Shenyang J-5 and Poland as the PZL-Mielec Lim-6.
NASA X-43: Boeing. The NASA X-43 was an experimental unmanned hypersonic aircraft with multiple planned scale variations meant to test various aspects of hypersonic flight.
Who is credited with discovering Phoenix?
Phoenix (constellation): Petrus Plancius. Named after the mythical phoenix, it was first depicted on a celestial atlas by Johann Bayer in his 1603 Uranometria.
Who is credited with discovering Glycerol?
Glycerol: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Glycerol is a sugar alcohol with chemical formula C3H5(OH)3.
Who is credited with discovering Theory of relativity?
Theory of relativity: Albert Einstein. Special relativity applies to all physical phenomena in the absence of gravity.
Who is credited with discovering Sombrero Galaxy?
Sombrero Galaxy: Pierre Méchain. It is a member of the Virgo II Groups, a series of galaxies and galaxy clusters strung out from the southern edge of the Virgo Supercluster.

Produced by the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex, this mineralocorticoid is the body's key sodium-saver, quietly governing blood pressure and potassium balance in the kidney — which hormone is it?
Aldosterone is the main mineralocorticoid steroid hormone produced by the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex in the adrenal gland.
This psychological term describes a diverse set of deficits in the ability to feel or anticipate pleasure, and is recognized as a diagnostic feature in the DSM-5 — what's the term?
Anhedonia is a diverse array of deficits in hedonic function, including reduced motivation or ability to experience pleasure.
Four novels and fifty-six short stories about a certain consulting detective made his name — but this knighted British writer-physician also invented Professor Challenger. Who was he?
Arthur Conan Doyle (22 May 1859 - 7 July 1930) was a British writer and physician.
Native to Europe, this small white-petaled, yellow-centered lawn flower is called 'common,' 'lawn,' or 'English' in various regions — what is its scientific name?
Bellis perennis (p-), the daisy, is a European species of the family Asteraceae, often considered the archetypal species of the name daisy.
This rigid, mineralized organ of the vertebrate skeleton produces both red and white blood cells and helps regulate the body's acid-base balance — what is it?
Bone is a rigid organ that constitutes part of the skeleton in most vertebrate animals.

What suborder of orthopteran insects — its Latin name meaning 'chisel-bearing,' after the stout shape of its members' egg-laying organs — includes grasshoppers, ground-hoppers, and pygmy mole crickets?
Caelifera are a suborder of orthopteran insects. The latter should not be confused with the mole crickets (Gryllotalpidae), which belong to the other Orthopteran suborder Ensifera.
Mature females are cows, the intact males are bulls, and the castrated males pull plows as oxen — all names for one widespread domesticated bovine kept as livestock. What animal is it?
Cattle (Bos taurus) are large, domesticated, bovid ungulates widely kept as livestock.
This roughly 24-hour internal biological cycle, generated within an organism but tuned by cues like daylight, is regulated by an internal biological clock — what is it called?
Circadian rhythm is a natural oscillation that repeats roughly every 24 hours.
Lending its metal to sterling silver, cupronickel coins, and strain-gauge alloys, this element carries atomic number 29 and a name drawn from the Latin 'cuprum' — what is it?
Copper is a chemical element; it has symbol Cu (from Latin cuprum) and atomic number 29.

This American nuclear physicist worked on the Manhattan Project and later led the Federation of American Scientists, best remembered for his 1959 testimony that helped sink a controversial cabinet nomination — who is he?
David L. Hill (November 11, 1919 - December 14, 2008) was an American nuclear physicist who worked on the Manhattan Project during World War II and was head of the Federation of American Scientists.
This scarab superfamily insect is famous for rolling balls of animal droppings, a behavior the Ancient Egyptians linked to the god Khepri — which creature is it?
Dung beetle are beetles that feed on feces.

This broad set of measures — taken by individuals, advocacy groups, and governments alike — aims to prevent pollution, conserve natural resources, and maintain ecological balance, sometimes repairing existing damage — what is it called?
Environmental protection refers to the taking of measures to protecting the natural environment, prevent pollution and maintain ecological balance.
A Swiss linguist and philosopher who died in 1913, this thinker's ideas shaped 20th-century linguistics, psychoanalysis, and anthropology alike, according to one of his translators — who is he?
Ferdinand de Saussure (26 November 1857 - 22 February 1913) was a Swiss linguist, semiotician and philosopher.

Discovered in Paris in 1875 and bearing the symbol Ga on the periodic table, this soft, silvery chemical element has such a low melting point — just below 30°C — that it turns liquid at warm room temperature. Name this element?
Gallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ga and atomic number 31.

Five species of this group of plants — rice, wheat, maize, barley, and sugar cane — together cover 46 percent of the world's arable land, alongside two related families, sedges and rushes. What kind of plant is this?
Grass refers to various families of plants.
Which 19th-century American economist's wildly popular treatise Progress and Poverty argued that a single tax on the value of land could build a more just and productive society?
Henry George (September 2, 1839 - October 29, 1897) was an American political economist, social philosopher and journalist.

In this heart condition, muscle tissue — most often in the wall between the ventricles — thickens for no obvious reason, weakening the heart's pumping and sometimes its electrical rhythm — name the condition?
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM, or HOCM when obstructive) is a condition in which muscle tissues of the heart become thickened without an obvious cause.

This Russian and Soviet physiologist discovered classical conditioning through famous experiments involving dogs, and won the 1904 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his separate research into digestion — who is he?
Holding doctorates in both anthropology and medicine, this SS physician earned the grim nickname 'Angel of Death' for his experiments and selections at Auschwitz — who was he?

Josef Mengele (16 March 1911 - 7 February 1979), often dubbed the "Angel of Death", was a German military officer and physician during World War II at the Soviet front and then at Auschwitz during the Holocaust.
This inflammation of the voice box causes symptoms ranging from a hoarse voice to complete voice loss, usually clearing up within two weeks. Name the condition?
Laryngitis is inflammation of the larynx (voice box). The primary symptom is loss of some vocal function, ranging from hoarse voice to no voice at all.
Used since pre-Columbian times as a pack animal that can haul about a quarter of its body weight for miles, which domesticated South American camelid has wool low in lanolin?
Llama (Spanish) (Lama glama) is a domesticated South American camelid, widely used as a meat and pack animal by Andean cultures since the pre-Columbian era.
Though it's the strongest bone in the face, this lower jawbone tends to deform with age and is prone to fractures — what is it called?

Mandible (from the Latin mandibula, 'for chewing'), lower jaw, or jawbone is a bone that makes up the lower - and typically more mobile - component of the mouth (the upper jaw being known as the maxilla).
Aristotle called this the 'first philosophy' — the branch that probes the most fundamental structure of reality, from existence itself to the categories of being — what is it?
Metaphysics is the branch of philosophy that examines the basic nature or most fundamental structure of reality.
Their name means "little fly" in Spanish, and biologists class them as micropredators — all sip flower nectar, but the females of many species also drink blood. What are they?
Mosquito are a family of small flies consisting of 3,600 species.

This Renaissance polymath put the Sun, not the Earth, at the center of the universe in a 1543 book published just before his death — likely arriving independently at an idea Aristarchus of Samos had floated eighteen centuries earlier. Who is he?
Nicolaus Copernicus (19 February 1473 - 24 May 1543) was a Renaissance polymath who formulated a model of the universe that placed the Sun rather than Earth at its center.
Many species in this cosmopolitan, often-fragrant family live as epiphytes on trees, and some have ditched leaves entirely — relying on highly specialized pollination tricks instead. What are they?
Orchid are plants that belong to the family Orchidaceae, a diverse and widespread group of flowering plants with blooms that are often colourful and fragrant.
This pulse crop, given the scientific name Pisum sativum by Linnaeus in 1753, is usually eaten as a vegetable via its small round seeds. What is it?
Pea is a pulse or fodder crop, but the word often refers to the seed or sometimes the pod of this flowering plant species.

A pnictogen with only one stable isotope and atomic number 15, this element hides in Earth's crust mostly as phosphate rock and readily builds a vast family of organic and inorganic compounds. Which element is it?
Phosphorus is a chemical element; it has symbol P and atomic number 15.
Part of the critical theory framework and closely tied to critical race theory, this field analyzes history, literature, and discourse shaped by imperial power — what field is it?

Postcolonialism is the academic study of the cultural, political and economic consequences of colonialism and imperialism, focusing on the impact of human control and exploitation of colonized people and their lands.

Found across Africa, Asia, and Australia, this family of nonvenomous snakes includes some of the world's largest and kills by coiling to suffocate rather than by injecting venom — what is the family called?

Pythonidae are a family of nonvenomous snakes found in Africa, Asia, and Australia. The taxonomy of pythons has evolved, and they are now known to be more closely related to sunbeam snakes and the Mexican burrowing python.
With a surface temperature over 12,000 Kelvin and a radius more than seventy times the Sun's, this blue supergiant is the brightest point of light in Orion — which star?
Rigel is a blue supergiant star in the equatorial constellation of Orion.
This systematic discipline builds testable explanations about nature and society, and is continuously challenged and validated by the community that practices it. What is it?
Science is a systematic discipline that builds and organises knowledge in the form of testable explanations about nature and society.
The brightest star in the night sky, this star sits in the constellation Canis Major and is actually a binary system paired with a faint white dwarf companion — name the star?
Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky, located in the southern constellation of Canis Major.

Held together by its own gravity, this luminous sphere of plasma is the type of object our Sun is, with roughly 4,000 of them visible to the naked eye on a clear night - what are these objects called?
Star is a luminous spheroid of plasma held together by self-gravity.
This genus of flowering plants in the daisy family is better known by the fluffy-seeded lawn weed it produces, with two European species now invasive nearly worldwide. What is it?
Taraxacum is a genus of flowering plants in the family Asteraceae which consists of species commonly known as dandelions.
This family of large, long-legged flies can be identified by a maxillary-palp segment longer than the other three combined, and typically has thirteen segments in each antenna. Name the family?
Tipulidae is a family of large crane flies in the order Diptera.
A physician before politics, this German served as Angela Merkel's defence minister and in 2019 became President of the European Commission — who is she?
Ursula von der Leyen (ne Albrecht; born 8 October 1958) is a German politician and physician who has served as President of the European Commission since 2019.
The first person to ever call himself a psychologist, this German founder of modern psychology launched Philosophische Studien, the field's first academic research journal — who is he?
Wilhelm Wundt (16 August 1832 - 31 August 1920) was a German physiologist, philosopher, professor, and one of the fathers of modern psychology.

Best known for the Cities of Salt quintet chronicling how oil discovery upended traditional Bedouin life, this novelist's criticism of Middle Eastern elites led Saudi Arabia to revoke his citizenship — who is he?

Originally launched in 2008 as Bombardier's CSeries, this five-abreast narrow-body airliner family was rebranded in 2018 after a European aerospace giant acquired a majority stake. What's it called today?
Airbus A220: Canadian narrow-body airliner family. The Airbus A220 is a family of five-abreast narrow-body airliners by Airbus Canada Limited Partnership (ACLP).
This three-star system includes Proxima, the closest star to the Sun, and shines as the third-brightest point in the night sky after Sirius and Canopus — which system?
Alpha Centauri: Star system in the Centaurus constellation.
Commonly called windflowers, which genus of the buttercup family is native to every continent except Australia, New Zealand, and Antarctica?
Anemone: Genus of flowering plants in the family Ranunculaceae.
Also nicknamed the cross spider or diadem spider for the white markings on its back, this orb-weaver is native to Europe but was introduced to North America — what species is it?

Araneus diadematus: Species of spider. The spider species Araneus diadematus is commonly called the European garden spider, cross orbweaver, diadem spider, orangie, cross spider, and crowned orb weaver.
The third-largest fish in its family, behind Siberian taimen and Pacific Chinook, this species is unusual for surviving spawning and returning to sea to breed again — which fish?
Atlantic salmon: Species of fish. The Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) is a species of ray-finned fish in the family Salmonidae.

Members of the family Ursidae walk flat on plantigrade paws tipped with five claws that can't retract — and though most eat meat, the giant panda among them is mostly herbivorous. What animal is this?
Made by combining phenol and acetone, this compound forms 65 to 70 percent of the world's polycarbonate plastics production — which chemical?
Bisphenol A: Chemical used in plastics, xenoestrogen.

Unlike most elements, this one is forged entirely by cosmic-ray spallation and supernovae rather than stellar fusion, and is mined from evaporite minerals like borax, mostly in Turkey — which element?
Boron: Chemical element with atomic number 5 (B)
Unlike benzodiazepines, this anti-anxiety medication doesn't cause sedation or dependence, and works through serotonin 5-HT1A receptors with a delayed onset of two to four weeks — which drug?
Buspirone: Medication used to treat anxiety disorders.
Native to the Americas, this plant genus in the nightshade family produces the fruits we call peppers, including sweet bell types and fiery chilies — what genus is it?
This bacterial skin infection affects the dermis and subcutaneous fat, most often striking the legs or face and causing spreading redness and swelling — what is it?
Cellulitis: Bacterial infection of the inner layers of the skin called the dermis.
Known for a bitter metallic aftertaste that gets worse if you rinse with water, this antiseptic is used before surgery and to prevent dental plaque — what is it?
Chlorhexidine: Disinfectant and antiseptic. Chlorhexidine is a disinfectant and antiseptic which is used for skin disinfection before surgery and to disinfect surgical instruments.
This process turns blood from liquid to gel through platelet activation and fibrin formation, beginning almost instantly after a vessel is injured — what's the clotting process called?
Coagulation: Process of formation of blood clots. Coagulation, also known as clotting, is the process by which blood changes from a liquid to a gel forming a blood clot.

This physician was convicted of involuntary manslaughter in 2011 after inadvertently overdosing his famous patient with the anesthetic propofol, which he had been improperly using as a sleep aid — who is he?
Conrad Murray: American physician and convicted felon (born 1953)
Native to the Andes and Mesoamerica, this plant genus includes five edible species known variously as squash, pumpkin or gourd — which genus?
Native to Madagascar and grown ornamentally throughout the tropics, this legume tree is known for its fern-like leaves and a flamboyant summer display of orange-red blossoms — what is it?
Delonix regia: Species of flowering plant in the bean family Fabaceae.
Bred in Córdoba in the early 1900s to hunt wild boar and puma, this large mastiff-type breed's ancestry includes an extinct local fighting dog and a Bull Terrier — which breed is it?
Dogo Argentino: Argentine breed of dog. It was bred in the early twentieth century in Córdoba in central Argentina, primarily for hunting large game such as peccaries, wild boar, and pumas.

A British physicist who hauled a captured German thermionic valve back from the Western Front, he won the 1947 Nobel for mapping the ionosphere — work that paved the way for radar and shortwave radio. Who was he?

Native across the arctic and temperate Northern Hemisphere, this fern relative grows both a spore-bearing stem and a separate sterile green one, and is often mistaken for mare's tail — what plant is it?
The only member of its family found outside the Americas, this tiny insect-eating bird holds its short tail erect and is unusually polygynous for a songbird — what is it?
Eurasian wren: Species of bird. In Anglophone Europe, it is commonly known simply as the wren.

Marked by widespread chronic pain plus fatigue and foggy thinking, this condition affects 2 to 4% of people, more often women, and was first recognised in the 1950s but only defined in 1990 — what is it?
Known for wood used in tool handles, electric guitars, and Morgan Motor Company's sports car frames, this tree genus produced nymphs called the Meliae in Greek myth — which genus?
Fraxinus: Genus of plants. The genus is widespread throughout much of Europe, Asia, and North America.
Called 'a bridge between the natural and social sciences,' this discipline studies Earth's lands, features, inhabitants, and how they all came to be — what is it?
Geography: Study of Earth's spatial information.
Supporting 249 languages and language varieties as of 2026, this Google service uses neural machine translation to convert text, documents and whole websites. Name it.
Google Translate is a multilingual neural machine translation service developed by Google for text, documents and websites. As of June 2026 it supports 249 languages and language varieties.
Created by a web server and stored by your browser, this small block of data is what lets a site remember your shopping basket or keep you logged in between page loads. What is it called?

An HTTP cookie is a small block of data a web server creates while a user browses a site, placed on the user's device by the browser, letting servers store stateful information such as items in a basket or whether the user is signed in.
Often contracted from undercooked shellfish or contaminated water, this foodborne viral liver disease causes symptoms like jaundice and fever that typically last around eight weeks — what is it?
Hepatitis A: Acute infectious disease of the liver.
This hormone, produced by cells surrounding a growing embryo, is what's detected in pregnancy tests and sometimes secreted by tumors, aiding cancer diagnosis — what is it?
Human chorionic gonadotropin: Hormone for the maternal recognition of pregnancy.

This crystalline mineral form of frozen water occurs naturally on Earth, other planets, and even in Oort cloud objects, and has at least nineteen known phases depending on temperature and pressure — what is it?
Ice: Frozen water; the solid state of water.

A theoretical physicist who studied under Max Born earned a chemistry degree from Harvard before pivoting to nuclear physics — and later oversaw the first atomic weapons during WWII. Who is this pivotal figure in physics history?
J. Robert Oppenheimer: American theoretical physicist (1904–1967)

The id Software programmer behind Wolfenstein 3D, Doom, and Quake later left to become CTO of Oculus VR — before walking away again to chase artificial general intelligence. Which 3D-graphics wizard is he?
John Carmack: American computer programmer and video game developer (born 1970)
Defined by a carbon-oxygen double bond flanked by two carbon groups, this class of organic compound includes acetone and gives some sugars and steroids like testosterone their structure — what is it?
Ketone: Organic compounds of the form >C=O.

This trigonometric relationship links each side of a triangle to the angle across from it, with every such ratio equal to twice the radius of the triangle's circumscribed circle. What is the rule called?
Law of sines: Property of all triangles on a Euclidean plane.
Patented in 1978 and approved for use in the US in 1987, this ACE inhibitor is a common first-line treatment for high blood pressure — what drug is it?
Lisinopril: Medication used to treat hypertension and heart failure.
Named from a Greek root meaning 'light' or 'brightness' in reference to its luminous, reflective eyes, this genus includes the bobcat among its four wild cat species — which genus?
Lynx: Genus of medium-sized wild cats.

Raising silkworms at 13 and publishing a two-volume study of caterpillars, this German-Dutch artist was among the earliest European naturalists to document insects from direct observation — who was she?
Maria Sibylla Merian: German naturalist and artist (1647–1717)
Also called pennyroyal, this minty flowering plant native to Europe, North Africa and the Middle East has a folk-remedy history despite being toxic to the liver — what species is it?

Given the NATO reporting name 'Hip,' this Soviet-designed helicopter family has been in continuous production since 1975 as a medium twin-turbine transport, with an armed gunship variant — which aircraft?
Mil Mi-17: Family of Russian military transport helicopters.

First identified from skulls found in a Dutch chalk quarry near Maastricht and initially mistaken for crocodile or whale bones, this giant marine lizard genus lived until 66 million years ago — which genus is it?
Mosasaurus: Extinct genus of marine lizard from the Late Cretaceous.
Divided in two by a central septum, this air-filled space sits behind the nose and forms the uppermost part of the respiratory system — what is it?
Nasal cavity: Large, air-filled space above and behind the nose in the middle of the face.
A catecholamine whose very name nods to the kidney, it acts as both a hormone and neurotransmitter and is called "noradrenaline" outside the US — what is it?
Norepinephrine: Catecholamine hormone and neurotransmitter. The general function of norepinephrine is to mobilize the brain and body for action.
Its Greek name means 'serpent-bearer,' and it's depicted as a man grasping a snake represented by a neighboring constellation — which constellation straddles the celestial equator?
Ophiuchus: Constellation straddling the celestial equator. Ophiuchus ( o-fee-YOO-kəs) is a large constellation straddling the celestial equator.
This butterfly was the first species to be given the common name now applied to its entire family, and is widespread across the Palearctic and North America — which species?
Papilio machaon: Species of insect. Papilio machaon, the Old World swallowtail, is a butterfly of the family Papilionidae.
This inflammation of the sac surrounding the heart causes sharp chest pain that eases when sitting up and worsens when lying down or breathing deeply — what condition is it?
Pericarditis: Inflammation of the pericardium. Pericarditis (PER-i-kar-DYE-tis) is inflammation of the pericardium, the fibrous sac surrounding the heart.
Boasting the longest cones of any spruce and widely planted as a Christmas tree, this European conifer was also the first gymnosperm to have its genome sequenced — which species?
Picea abies: Species of plant. Picea abies, the Norway spruce, Norway fir or European spruce, is a species of spruce native to Northern, Central and Eastern Europe.
Born Joseph Ratzinger, this head of the Catholic Church made history in 2013 by resigning the role, then adopted the title 'emeritus' until his death — who was he?
Pope Benedict XVI: Head of the Catholic Church from 2005 to 2013.

With 348 known species spanning an opportunistic human pathogen, a plant disease-causer, and a soil-dwelling growth-promoter, which gram-negative bacterial genus in Gammaproteobacteria is renowned for its metabolic diversity?
Pseudomonas: Genus of Gram-negative bacteria. Pseudomonas is a genus of gram-negative bacteria belonging to the family Pseudomonadaceae in the class Gammaproteobacteria.
This Norwegian shared the very first Nobel Memorial Prize in Economics, and we owe him the words 'econometrics,' 'microeconomics,' and 'macroeconomics' — who was he?
Ragnar Frisch: Norwegian economist and Nobel Laureate (1895–1973)
Native to Europe, northwestern Africa, and southwestern Asia, this flowering shrub's edible fruit stars in desserts and preserves — what's its species name, better known as the gooseberry?
Ribes uva-crispa: Species of flowering plant in the family Grossulariaceae.
Introduced in the 1970s, this database language let programmers grab many records with one single command, eliminating the need to specify an index path to reach each one — what is it?

Originally from the Mediterranean, this yellowish-gray arthropod has up to 15 pairs of long legs and preys on insects with venom too mild to harm humans — what species commonly invades homes worldwide?
Scutigera coleoptrata: Species of arthropod. Scutigera coleoptrata, also known as the house centipede, is a species of centipede that is typically yellowish-gray and has up to 15 pairs of long legs.
Better known by the brand name Viagra, this drug treats erectile dysfunction and pulmonary arterial hypertension, kicking in within about twenty minutes — what is it?

Sildenafil: Drug for erectile dysfunction and hypertension. Sildenafil, sold under the brand name Viagra among others, is a medication used to treat erectile dysfunction and pulmonary arterial hypertension.
Native to East Asia and the world's most-grown legume, this crop becomes everything from edamame and tofu to soy sauce, nattō and tempeh — what is it?
Soybean: Legume grown for its edible bean.
A member of the rose family, this bright red treat is botanically not a berry at all, and each of its 'seeds' on the outside is really a tiny fruit called an achene — what is it?
Strawberry: Edible fruit. The garden strawberry (or simply strawberry; Fragaria × ananassa) is a widely grown hybrid plant cultivated worldwide for its fruit.
Named by Linnaeus in 1753 but called cempōhualxōchitl by the Nahua long before, this genus of Mexican-native flowers is commonly known as marigolds — what's the genus?

Taught in universities and seminaries, this academic discipline studies religious belief from within a religious perspective, focusing on divinity, revelation, and how God might interact with the world — what field is it?
Theology: Study of the nature of deities and religious beliefs.
This field of geoscience studies the shape of land surfaces — not just elevation, but roads, boundaries, and buildings too, as shown on USGS terrain maps — what is it called?
Topography: Study of the forms of land surfaces in earth.

This late Cretaceous carnivore, whose scientific name pairs a word for 'tyrant' with the Latin for 'king,' roamed western North America right up until the mass extinction 66 million years ago — which iconic predator is it?
Tyrannosaurus: Genus of Late Cretaceous theropod.
Every snake in this venomous family wields unusually long, hinged fangs for deep envenomation — and many give live birth, a trait echoed in their Latin-rooted name. What snakes are these?
Viper: Family of snakes. The earliest known vipers are believed to have diverged from the rest of the clade Caenophidia in the early Eocene.

This Turkish academic and bureaucrat earned his doctorate at George Washington University and now directs Türkiye's National Intelligence Organization after years as Erdoğan's spokesperson — who is he?
İbrahim Kalın: Turkish bureaucrat and Islamic studies scholar.
Francium is denoted by which symbol?

Paw Patrol: The Mighty Movie: 2024. Paw Patrol: The Mighty Movie is a 2023 Canadian animated superhero film based on the television series Paw Patrol.
